name: Pulmonary Artery Sarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of an intraluminal mass in the pulmonary artery on imaging studies
Histopathological confirmation of sarcomatous tumor cells from biopsy or surgical specimen
Clinical and radiological features mimicking chronic pulmonary thromboembolism but unresponsive to anticoagulation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus imaging evidence of pulmonary artery mass
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often delayed due to clinical similarity to pulmonary embolism.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pulmonary artery intraluminal mass detected on imaging

laboratory: Non-specific elevation of inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP)
imaging: CT pulmonary angiography showing intraluminal filling defect with mass characteristics
MRI demonstrating heterogeneous mass with contrast enhancement in pulmonary artery
PET-CT showing increased metabolic activity in pulmonary artery lesion
genetic: No well-established genetic markers; occasional MDM2 amplification reported
other: Histopathology showing spindle cell sarcoma with immunohistochemical staining positive for vimentin and variable expression of smooth muscle actin

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of mass lesion on imaging
Different hemodynamic profile on right heart catheterization
Thrombus rather than tumor on imaging

redFlags: Persistent pulmonary artery filling defect despite anticoagulation
Rapid progression of symptoms mimicking pulmonary embolism
Evidence of intraluminal mass on advanced imaging
references: Blackmon SH, et al. Pulmonary artery sarcoma: a review. Ann Thorac Surg. 2009;87(3):977-985.
Bandyopadhyay D, et al. Pulmonary artery sarcoma: a close mimic of pulmonary thromboembolism. Indian J Radiol Imaging. 2016;26(2):193-196.
Kawano O, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary artery sarcoma. Ann Thorac Cardiovasc Surg. 2017;23(3):121-127.
